comparison: Perfect agreement on mechanical findings (C17, C31-C38, C45-C49). Both evaluations find strong support for viscoelastic effects on skin mechanics with compelling quantitative evidence. OpenEval emphasizes specific variability measurements while peer reviewers praise the elegant design and accurate measurements.

Perfect agreement on SA-2 findings (C5, C21-C22, C66-C71). Both evaluations support the population analysis and continuous signaling claims. Peer reviewers specifically note the thorough SA-2 analysis as particularly noteworthy, aligning with OpenEval's assessment of strong evidence from multidimensional scaling and Procrustes alignment.

Perfect agreement on methodological claims (C23-C26, C110-C122). Both evaluations find the methods well-designed and appropriate. OpenEval describes them as well-documented with justified procedures, while peer reviewers praise the elegant design, thorough control of forces/displacements, and large dataset as strengths.

Perfect agreement on interpretive claims about SA-2 functional roles (C92-C99). Both evaluations support these interpretations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative functional claims not directly tested, while peer reviewers accept them as reasonable interpretations that provoke further questions and support the conclusions.

Strong agreement on background and foundational claims (C7-C16, C27). Both evaluations support these as well-established knowledge. OpenEval notes they are well-supported by citations, while peer reviewers accept them without question as appropriately framing the study with well-explained context.

Strong agreement on neural variability findings (C3, C18, C39-C43). Both evaluations find strong support for increased firing rate variability across neuron types. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and parallel with mechanical variability, while peer reviewers confirm compelling evidence for impact on neural coding of force.

Strong agreement on information-theoretic analysis and neuron heterogeneity (C4, C19-C20, C53-C62). Both evaluations support the classification of neurons and reduction in information transmission. OpenEval highlights data-driven validation, while peer reviewers praise advanced analysis methods applied to large dataset revealing dynamic coding properties.

Strong agreement on neuron-type differences (C83-C89). Both evaluations support differential effects across neuron types. OpenEval notes partial slip explanations are more speculative though consistent with literature, while peer reviewers accept mechanistic explanations based on known receptor properties without challenge.

Strong agreement on regression analysis findings (C50, C79-C82, C90-C91). Both evaluations support the interaction model and analytical techniques. OpenEval notes varying prediction accuracy indicates complexity not fully captured, while peer reviewers praise analytical techniques and confirm results support conclusions about neural coding.

Agreement on main conclusions (C6, C72, C102) with different emphasis. Both evaluations support the primary findings. OpenEval finds them well-supported by convergence of multiple approaches, while peer reviewers explicitly endorse that authors achieved their aims and results support conclusions. Peer evaluation also includes speculative claims C103-C105.

Agreement on foundational viscoelastic claims (C1, C2, C11). Both evaluations support these as established knowledge. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with experimental observations, while peer reviewers accept them as appropriate background framing without question. Peer evaluation covers broader background claims.

Partial overlap on speculative functional claims. OpenEval rates C100-C101, C103-C105 as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental support, while peer reviewers support broader implications (C6, C72, C102-C105) as reasonable interpretations that adequately outline importance and scope.

Agreement on contextual claims about fingertip function (C106-C109). OpenEval supports C106-C108 as well-established knowledge and C109 as reasonable speculation, while peer reviewers accept broader implications and adequately outlined importance. Both treat these interpretive claims favorably.

Divergent assessment of speculative claims (C76-C78). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are interpretive and speculative without direct experimental support though consistent with literature. Peer reviewers support these claims as part of adequately outlined importance and scope, accepting broader implications.

OpenEval evaluated stimulus parameter claims (C28-C30) as SUPPORTED with direct protocol support and physiologically relevant justification. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological details.
